title: Publication 527 (2025), Residential Rental Property (Including Rental of Vacation Homes)
entity_roles: Individual with mixed personal and rental use
source_classification: Official IRS interpretive tax publication, not financial accounting GAAP
inspected_summary: The publication treats rent and refundable tenant deposits differently for income-tax purposes, calls for separate repair and improvement records, and divides mixed rental/personal expenses under the selected use rules. It also discusses basis and depreciation records for rental property. The controller should keep use, lease, deposit and capital-project evidence separate; actual return treatment depends on facts and tax year.
locators: Special Situations: Personal Use of Dwelling Unit

title: Publication 551 (12/2025), Basis of Assets
source_classification: Official IRS interpretive tax publication, not financial accounting GAAP
inspected_summary: Basis is used for tax depreciation and disposition calculations; acquisition costs and later adjustments require retained evidence. Tax basis is not automatically the value used in a family net-worth presentation or other financial-reporting basis.

title: A Consumer's Guide to Home Insurance
jurisdictions: United States, general consumer insurance practice
accounting_bases: Insurance claims documentation; no accounting measurement rule
source_classification: Insurance regulator association practical consumer guide; not binding accounting guidance
inspected_summary: The guide distinguishes homeowner, personal-property and liability coverage, policy limits and insured replacement cost from market value. It recommends retaining policies and correspondence, a secure inventory of valuable possessions with photographs, and receipts for repairs and acquisitions to support claims. It does not determine accounting fair value or insurance adequacy for a particular family.
locators: PDF pp. 6, 9-10, 15-16 (printed pp. 1, 4-5, 10-11): coverages, limits, optional coverage, responsibilities and claim records

evidence.method: original publisher PDF direct open and selected page inspection
evidence.observed: Guide separates policy replacement cost and market value, addresses personal-asset endorsements, and describes secure inventory, receipts and claim documentation.

title: Blueprint: Accounting for Leases Under ASC 842
source_classification: Professional interpretive handbook on ASC 842; examples and guidance are not authoritative Codification text
inspected_summary: The 2026 handbook’s lessor summary states that operating-lease payments are generally recognized straight-line over the lease term if collection is probable, with variable lease payments recognized when relevant facts/circumstances occur (or collected where collectibility is not probable). Its presentation section describes the lessor’s underlying assets/depreciation and current/noncurrent rent receivable and deferred rent balances.

title: Deloitte Roadmap: Leases, § 6.1 “General,” refundable and nonrefundable deposits
publication_date_or_edition: DART page accessed 2026-09-23; 2026 copyright shown; specific edition date not displayed in inspected passage
source_classification: Professional interpretation of ASC 842 lease-payment concepts; not the Codification itself
inspected_summary: Deloitte’s interpretation distinguishes refundable deposits (not lease payments while returnable) from nonrefundable deposits (fixed consideration). Applying a refundable deposit to rent arrears settles unpaid lease payments; retention for damage or other breach is generally a variable lease payment. Contract rights and actual reason for retention are essential.
